[P02] Missed radiology findings were substantially mitigated after the introduction of AI-assisted second-read protocols, with false-negative rates for pulmonary nodules falling by 58 percent.

[P03] Automation bias intensified as reliance on clinical decision support tools grew, with physicians less likely to override erroneous flagging compared with the pre-implementation era.

[P04] The implementation of structured handover checklists curtailed the incidence of missed diagnoses in the emergency department, with diagnostic discordance rates dropping from 8.3 to 2.1 percent over the trial period.

[P05] Delayed diagnoses of sepsis were largely abated after the electronic alert system was calibrated to flag borderline lactate values; door-to-antibiotic time improved by 47 minutes.

[P06] Procurement of a mobile CT unit enabled stroke imaging in rural ambulances, cutting the median time from symptom onset to treatment by 34 minutes.
